subject: art-design
title: Final Outcome: Foundations
welcome_lead: Plan a final piece that pulls together every stage of your project.
meta_desc: GCSE final outcome foundations: refining ideas, brief, media choice, planning.
final_note: A strong outcome looks inevitable because it was planned.

concepts.def: The starting prompt or theme to respond to.
The resolved piece that ends a project.
Improving an idea through repeated testing.
Deciding which materials best suit the idea.
How elements are arranged in the final piece.
A written or drawn map of what will be made.

walkthroughs.body_html: Before planning, read the original brief again. List the keywords. Your outcome should clearly answer the brief — not just be your favourite drawing. Highlight the words you want your final piece to physically embody.

If your idea is about delicacy and memory, watercolour fits better than acrylic impasto. Make a chart: idea on one side, media options on the other, pros and cons of each. Choose because, not by default.
Sketch the composition at small scale, list the materials, estimate time per stage and identify risks. A clear plan keeps you on track and lets you justify decisions later in your evaluation.
